title: Demonstrate an understanding of the role of water for poultry production

lessons.title: Why water matters to chickens
lessons.html:
Why water matters to chickens

Water is the most important nutrient for chickens. A chicken can live for some time without feed, but without water it gets sick and dies quickly, especially on a hot day. Chickens drink more water than they eat feed.

What water does in the body

  • It helps the bird eat and digest feed. Birds that cannot drink stop eating.
  • It cools the bird. Chickens cannot sweat, so they pant to lose heat, and this uses water.
  • It carries food and waste through the body.
  • An egg is mostly water, so layers need a lot of water to lay.

When birds need more water

  • On hot days birds drink much more.
  • As birds grow they drink more each day.
  • Layers drink more when they are laying well.

Signs that birds are short of water

  • Birds crowd around drinkers.
  • Birds eat less feed.
  • Birds pant and look weak.
  • Fewer eggs are laid.
  • Dry, sticky droppings.

If you see these signs, check the water at once and tell your supervisor.

Water and medicine

Vaccines and medicines are often given in the drinking water. The vet or supervisor decides this. Never add anything to the water on your own. Some cleaning products in the water can kill vaccines. Follow the instructions you are given exactly.

Measuring water

Many houses have a water meter. Read it at the same time each day and write the number in the record book. A sudden drop in water use is often the first sign of disease or a blocked line. A big rise can mean a leak or very hot weather.

lessons.title: Keeping water clean and drinkers working
lessons.html:
Keeping water clean and drinkers working

Water must be clean, cool and always there. Dirty water spreads disease from bird to bird.

Types of drinkers

DrinkerWhat to check
Nipple linesWater comes out when pressed, no leaks, correct height
Bell drinkersWater level right, clean inside, hanging level
Fonts (chick drinkers)Filled, clean, not tipped over

Daily drinker checks

  1. Check every line or drinker on each round.
  2. Press a few nipples on each line, including at the far end.
  3. Look for leaks and wet litter under drinkers. Wet litter causes sore feet, smells of ammonia and grows germs.
  4. Clean bell drinkers and fonts every day. Scrub out dirt, feed and droppings.
  5. Raise drinkers as birds grow. Nipple lines are usually set so birds stretch up slightly to drink.

Water supply

  • Keep header tanks and reservoirs covered so dust, birds and rats cannot get in.
  • In hot weather, flush lines so warm water is replaced with cooler water. Birds drink less when water is hot.
  • Tell your supervisor if the water looks dirty, smells bad or the borehole pump is not working.

Use water wisely

South Africa is a dry country. Fix or report leaking taps and pipes quickly. Do not leave hoses running. Wasted water costs the farm money.

Key points

  • Water is the most important nutrient; chickens need it all the time.
  • Birds drink more when hot, growing or laying.
  • Check and clean drinkers every day and fix leaks.
  • Never add medicine or chemicals to water on your own.
  • Read the water meter daily and report big changes.
